subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB391.md - CLOSED. 14.9.25.4 GR11 ('the same as if the user had referred to each pair of corresponding identifiers in separate MOVE statements') is right only if the SET of pairs is right, which is 14.7.6's question and is recorded in full on SR-14.9.25.3-13. NOTE 5's group descent was always there, and the reason nested national and bit group members were silently DROPPED was the deleted private Table-16 copy's '_ => false' default for national and boolean SENDERS. Re-measured at 2023 after that deletion: a nested national group's PIC N(3) child moves (NA2=[XYZ] where it read QQQ), a nested bit group's PIC 1(4) child moves (BO2=[1010] where it read 0000), and the complementary OVER-match is gone (NV2 keeps QQQ), which is the verdict MoveTable16 gives the DIRECT move. THE RESIDUAL RECORDED HERE IS NOW CLOSED TOO: rule 2's non-table half - 14.9.25.3 SR8 and SR9, the two rules SR10 explicitly defers to - is asked, so the implied MOVE GR11 emits is one the MOVE statement's own rules admit. A BINARY-CHAR/-SHORT/-LONG/-DOUBLE sender no longer pairs with a non-numeric namesake receiver (conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb391_corresponding_rule2_sr8_binary), and a variable-length-group namesake no longer pairs with an elementary one in either direction - that pair used to emit an implied MOVE whose whole-group image does not exist and threw NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time, which is the sharpest statement available that the pair set was wrong (conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb391_corresponding_rule2_sr9_varlen). Both go through the one composite entry MoveTable16.DataItemRefusal. At 85 the national and boolean operands are themselves COBOL0900-gated and the COBOL-85-expressible half is pinned by conformance:cases/14.7.6-CORRESPONDING/pb391_corresponding_rule2_table16_85; SR8's introducing edition is 2002 (the binary-char/-short/-long/-double usages) and SR9's is 2014 (DYNAMIC LENGTH 13.18.19 / OCCURS format 4 13.18.38), which is where each golden sits. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/MoveTable16.cs#Refusal (kb/Work PB2076 moved Table 16 to the runtime as MoveValidity.Table16Refusal, which MoveTable16's chain (DataItemRefusal) asks)
